title: Diabetes, hypertension and CKD together
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for renal maintenance and diabetes management.

HPI
The patient is a 66-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his chronic kidney disease. He is currently on maintenance hemodialysis and reports that his treatments have been consistent. He also manages type 2 diabetes through diet modifications alone and currently takes no medications for glucose control. He reports stable hypertension and denies any new symptoms of fluid overload or significant fatigue since his last visit.

Medication List
Antihypertensive medication (generic)
Dietary management for T2DM

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Blood pressure is 132/78 mmHg. Heart rate is 72 bpm. Lungs are clear to auscultation. No peripheral edema is noted.

Assessment
1. End stage renal disease: The patient’s most recent laboratory work shows an eGFR of 12 mL/min/1.73m2.
2. Hypertension: Currently stable on current regimen.
3. Type 2 diabetes: Managed via diet.

Plan
Continue current hemodialysis schedule. Continue current antihypertensive medication. Monitor renal function and blood pressure at next visit.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes and CKD are linked by the 'with' convention unless the provider says otherwise: E11.22 (HCC 37).
Hypertension with CKD stage 5 or ESRD: I12.0 (HCC 326).
The CKD stage is coded in addition: N18.6.

distractors.why: The 'with' convention presumes the diabetes caused the CKD.
I12.9 is for stage 1-4 or unspecified CKD.
Hypertension and CKD are presumed linked: I12.-, not I10.
E11.22 says to use an additional code for the CKD stage.
Dialysis status is reported with Z99.2.
